rv.q: In Dame Judi Dench's majestically authoritative interpretation, this beacon of good sense radiates a single-minded dignity.
Wanamaker, sprawled over a sofa in humiliating self-abasement, performs the piece with a soul-baring virtuosity that transcends the material and confirms that the Branagh season is devoted to actors.
There’s a nice balance in this Terence Rattigan double bill, as close to ‘perfect’ as it is humanly possible to get.
I was smiling throughout and the audience roared with appreciation at the end.

Harlequinade Running at around 70 minutes, this light comedy complements the other two pieces, with its allusions to The Winter's Tale and Romeo and Juliet . It is an early precursor of Noises Off which takes place as a touring theatre company of startlingly low quality puts the final touches to its new run of R & J.

cn.t: Critics praise this Terence Rattigan double bill as a delightful theatrical treat, with Zoë Wanamaker's monologue performance earning particular acclaim and the farce offering charming, well-executed light relief.
